metadata.description: REGISTRY DATA ERROR: This pair was curated to compare Roth (1953) 'On Certain Sets of Integers' (paper342) against Behrend (1946) 'On Sets of Integers Which Contain No Three Terms in Arithmetical Progression' (paper341), with hypothesised relation CF (Behrend's lower bound construction vs Roth's matching upper bound). However, BOTH source PDFs at paper341 and paper342 are in fact the SAME paper: Erdos & Turan 1936, 'On Some Sequences of Integers', J. London Math. Soc. Vol. 11. Both extractions document this registry mismatch in metadata.registry_mismatch_note. Comparing a paper to itself does not yield a meaningful Roth-vs-Behrend alignment, so we mark NEG. The two extractions are essentially the same content (definitions of A-sequence and r(N), Theorem I r(2N) <= N+1 (or N) for N>=8, Theorem II density bound near 3/8 or 1/2, the same proofs by induction with reflection/translation/subadditivity, the same base cases r(8)=4 .. r(14)=8 and r(17)=8, the same r(41)=16 witness, the same Szekeres conjecture and ternary construction). Match entries below pair the trivially-corresponding nodes for completeness, but the pair itself contributes no signal about Roth vs Behrend; the underlying source data needs to be re-fetched.

matches.explanation: Both papers (which are the same Erdos-Turan 1936 paper) define an A-sequence in [1,N] as an increasing integer sequence with no three terms in arithmetic progression. Identical statement up to whitespace.
Both define r(N) as the maximum length of an A-sequence belonging to N. Identical.
Both define the generalized r_l(N) = largest subset of {1,...,N} with no l-term arithmetic progression. Identical.

Same Theorem I (linear upper bound r(2N) <= N+1 or N for N>=8). Paper341 states r(2N) <= N+1; paper342 states r(2N) <= N. Both are extractions of the same Erdos-Turan Theorem I; the off-by-one discrepancy reflects OCR/extraction noise rather than a substantive difference. Confidence high because both extractions clearly target the same theorem.

Same Theorem II (asymptotic density bound r(N) < (c+epsilon)N for large N). Paper341 reconstructed the constant as c = 3/8, paper342 reconstructed it as c = 1/2; both extractions explicitly flag this as OCR-reconstructed (the original Erdos-Turan 1936 constant is 1/2, so paper342 is correct; paper341's 3/8 is an extraction error). The theorem itself is the same. Confidence medium due to the OCR-induced constant discrepancy.
Same reflection invariance fact: a_i -> N+1-a_i preserves the A-sequence property. Paper341 typed it as equation, paper342 as lemma; cross-type but identical content.
Same translation invariance fact: a_i -> a_i - k preserves the A-sequence property. Cross-type (equation vs lemma) but identical content.
Subadditivity of r: r(m+n) <= r(m) + r(n). Identical statement in both extractions.

Paper341 collected all small-N exact values into a single lemma LP341.2 (covering r(8)..r(14), plus r(17)=8 and r(18)..r(23) and r(41)=16). Paper342 split this into three lemmas: LP342.4 (r(8)..r(14)), LP342.5 (r(17)=8 and consequences r(34),r(35) etc.), and LP342.6 (r(18)=r(19)=r(20)=8, r(21)=9, r(22)=r(23)=9). Many-to-one match reflects extraction granularity choice.

Proof of Theorem I: induction on N using reflection/translation symmetry, subadditivity, and small-base cases. Both extractions describe the same induction skeleton. Inner step DAGs (PSP341.1-5 vs PSP342.1-8) align as described in the composite step entry below.

Composite L2 alignment of the Theorem I proof steps. Paper342's decomposition is finer: PSP342.1 (reflection setup) ~ PSP341.1; PSP342.2 (translation setup) ~ PSP341.1; PSP342.3 (subadditivity application) ~ PSP341.2; PSP342.4-6 (base cases r(8), r(10), r(12) split into three steps) ~ PSP341.3 (collected as one) and PSP341.4 (r(14)=r(13)=...); PSP342.7 (subadditive corollaries r(16),r(18),r(20),r(22)) ~ tail of PSP341.4; PSP342.8 (induction step) ~ PSP341.5. Same proof, different chunking.

Proof of Theorem II: derive r(17)=8, deduce r(34)<=16 and r(35)<=16, iterate the doubling-with-forbidden-midpoint to get r(2^{k+2}+/-2^{k-1}-1) bounds, refine via r(18)..r(23) values. Both extractions describe the same chain.

Composite L2 alignment of the Theorem II proof steps. PSP341.6 (show r(17)=8) ~ PSP342.9; PSP341.7 (deduce r(34)<=16, r(35)<=16) ~ PSP342.10; PSP341.8 (iterate doubling) ~ PSP342.11; paper342 has an additional refinement step PSP342.12 (r(18)..r(23), gets the tighter 1/2+epsilon constant) which paper341 folded into PSP341.8.
Identical witness A-sequence 1,2,4,5,10,11,13,14,28,29,31,32,37,38,40,41 in [1,41] showing r(41)=16. Same example.
Ternary-no-digit-2 construction giving r((3^k+1)/2) >= 2^k. Paper341 typed as example, paper342 as remark. Same construction.
Szekeres conjecture (l=3 case): r((3^k+1)/2) = 2^k, verified for k=1,2,3,4.

General Szekeres conjecture for r_l. Both extractions flag the LHS index expression as OCR-garbled and reconstruct it as a (p^k - 2p^{k-1} + ...)/(p-1) formula, with RHS (p-1)^k. Same conjecture, both partially reconstructed.
Same open problem: probably r(N) = o(N). Both notes mention this was settled by Roth (1953).
Same consequence: Szekeres' conjecture would imply infinitely many k-term arithmetic progressions of primes.
Same conditional improved van der Waerden bound f(k,l) <= l^{e^{k log k}} from Szekeres' conjecture. Paper341 typed as remark, paper342 typed as theorem; both flag the exponent as OCR-reconstructed.

Paper341 explicitly extracted the van der Waerden number f(k,l) as a separate (external-origin) definition; paper342 mentioned it inline within TP342.3 rather than splitting it out. Granularity-only difference.

Paper341 extracted van der Waerden's theorem as a separate external-origin theorem node; paper342 referred to it implicitly within TP342.3. External-origin so does not affect relation_type; listed for completeness.

Paper342 added a sharpness remark for Theorem I (r(2N) <= N holds for N=4,5,6 but fails for N=7); paper341 incorporated this implicitly into the case-analysis discussion of Theorem I rather than as a standalone remark.
